publishedfiledetails.title: Combined Status
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
[h1]Supports all versions of Don't Starve ([url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=574636989]Vanilla, Reign of Giants, Shipwrecked, Hamlet[/url], Don't Starve Together).[/h1]

[h2]You can also download from [url=https://github.com/rezecib/Combined-Status/releases]GitHub[/url], although that won't auto-update for you. (code contributions also welcome via GitHub)[/h2]

This mod enhances the HUD to better show the player's stats and various information about the world, such as temperature, season, and moon phase.

This is a client-only mod, so whoever has enabled it will see the changes, and whoever doesn't won't, regardless of what server you're on and whether the server has the mod or not.

Note that unlike Kiopho's Always On Status, I use the game's temperature units directly here, so player temperature can safely vary from 0-70, with freezing/overheating warnings occurring at 5 and 65. (you can change it to C, which works like Kiopho's version, or F if you want)

Credits to Kiopho ([url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=180843799]Always On Status[/url]), Soilworker ([url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=298407615]Season Clock[/url]), and hotmatrixx ([url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=292558919]Better Moon[/url]) for making the original mods. I completely rewrote all of the code to be more compatible, aesthetic, and easily maintained going forward.

[h1]Configuration Options[/h1]

[table]
[tr][td][h1]Option[/h1][/td][td][h1]Description[/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Temperature[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the temperature of the player. Defaults to [i]Show[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show World Temp[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the temperature of the world. Defaults to [i]Hide[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Temp Badges[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show small images to indicate which temperature is which. Badges only get shown if this is set to [i]Show[/i] and both player and world temperatures are enabled. Defaults to [i]Show[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Temperature Unit[/h1][/td][td]Whether to use the game's internal units (default), or approximations of Fahrenheit or Celsius.
[list][*] In [i]Game Units[/i], the player freezes at 0 and overheats at 70, with warning occurring 5 away.
[*] In [i]Celsius[/i], the player freezes at 0 and overheats at 35, with warning occurring 2.5 degrees away.
[*] In [i]Fahrenheit[/i], the player freezes at 32 and overheats at 95, with warning occurring 4.5 degrees away.
[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Waning[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show if the moon is waxing or waning by adding new icons. Defaults to [i]Show[/i]. (The game normally only shows icons for one direction). In Don't Starve Together, this is now a feature of the main game, so the option doesn't do anything.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Moon[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the moon only at [i]Night[/i] (the game's default), during night and dusk ([i]Dusk[/i], the mod's default), or [i]Always[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Predict Full Moon[/h1][/td][td]Whether to predict the day of the next full moon, shown when hovering over the moon icon. Defaults to [i]Yes[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Flip Moon[/h1][/td][td]Whether to flip the moon phase icon to show it like it is in the Southern Hemisphere, instead of the default Northern Hemisphere. Defaults to [i]No[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Season Clock[/h1][/td][td][i]Clock[/i], the default, shows a full clock of the seasons. [i]Compact[/i] shows a smaller badge with the season and day count, while [i]Micro[/i] shows an even smaller badge. [i]No[/i] disables the season clock entirely.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Naughtiness[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the naughtiness of the player. Doesn't work in Don't Starve Together (unless [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2189004162]Insight[/url] is installed), as  naughtiness is not available to clients. Defaults to [i]Show[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Log Meter[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the log meter for Woodie when he is human. Only relevant to singleplayer, as Don't Starve Together always shows the log meter already. Defaults to [i]Always[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Cave Clock[/h1][/td][td]Whether to always show the clock in the caves. Only relevant to singleplayer Reign of Giants, as the data is not available in vanilla and the clock shows in Don't Starve Together. Defaults to [i]Show[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Stat Numbers[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the sanity, hunger, and health numbers without having to mouse over the badges. Defaults to [i]Always[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Max Text[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show the "Max:" text when hovering over the sanity, hunger, and health badges to see their maximum values. Defaults to [i]Show[/i].[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Clock Text[/h1][/td][td]Whether to show text on the Clock and Season Clock. Defaults to [i]Show[/i]. If set to [i]Hide[/i], text will only be shown when mousing over or opening the Controller Inventory.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]HUD Scale[/h1][/td][td]Lets you adjust the size of the badges and clocks independently of the game's HUD scale. Defaults to [i]1[/i].[/td][/tr]
[/table]

publishedfiledetails.title: Global Positions
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
[h1]Map sharing works again! You don't even need to be in the  [b]A New Reign beta[/b] anymore![/h1]

Code contributions are welcome: https://github.com/rezecib/Global-Positions

[h1]Features[/h1]
[list]
[*] Show other players on the map (and hover over them to see who they are).
[*] Show player indicators (the bubble things on the side of the screen) when they're far away.
[*] Light signal fires that show up as indicators and on the map.
[*] Ping the map by alt+clicking, creating markers that show other players points of interest. Note that muting a player hides their pings. Controller users can ping by clicking in the right stick.
[*] Opt-out of sharing your location with a button on the scoreboard.
[*] Share your map discovery with other players automatically
[/list]

[h1]Wilderness Mode[/h1]
By default, if you play in Wilderness Mode, it will ignore most of the config options. If you want to override that, set the Wilderness Mode Override to Enabled. Otherwise, it will hide player positions, but always show campfires.

[h1]Configuration Options[/h1]
On the mods screen, with this mod selected, you can change a lot of the settings with the "Configure" button.
[table]
[tr][td][h1]Player Indicators[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Always[/u][/b] makes it so player indicators always show. [*][b][u]Scoreboard[/u][/b] (default) only shows them when you bring up the scoreboard. [*][b][u]Disabled[/u][/b] removes both the indicators and the map icons.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Player Icons[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Show[/u][/b] (default) will show player's map icons on the map. [*][b][u]Hide[/u][/b] will hide them.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Fires[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Always[/u][/b] means they always produce smoke signals when they're lit, so show up globally regardless of fuel used. [*][b][u]Charcoal[/u][/b] (default) means you have to fuel them with charcoal to produce smoke signals. [*][b][u]Disabled[/u][/b] turns off smoke signals entirely.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Fire Icons[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Show[/u][/b] (default) shows fire icons on the map when they are smoking.[*][b][u]Hide[/u][/b] doesn't show them even if they're smoking[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Share Map[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Enabled[/u][/b] (default) makes it so that as other players explore the world, your map will update too. Note that this will only work if players or icons are set to be shown.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Wilderness Override[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Disabled[/u][/b] (default) makes it so that in Wilderness Mode, [b]Show Fires[/b] is set to [b]Always[/b], and [b]Player Icons[/b] and [b]Player Indicators[/b] are [b]Disabled[/b]. This adds some risk of discovery to making fires, so cook with caution! [*][b][u]Enabled[/u][/b] makes it use whatever settings you have set yourself, rather than that Wilderness preset.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Pings[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Enabled[/u][/b] (default) allows players to alt+click the map to ping areas for others to see. [*][b][u]Disabled[/u][/b] doesn't allow pings at all.[/list][/td][/tr]
[/table]

Most options are only used by the host; if you're joining, the only option that gets read is whether to show the player indicators at all times or only on the scoreboard.


A huge thanks to Sarcen for figuring out his very clever system for getting player icons to show on the map globally for clients!

publishedfiledetails.title: Geometric Placement
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
[h1]Compatible with all versions of the game (Vanilla, Reign of Giants, Shipwrecked, Don't Starve Together-- separately listed on the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=356043883]Single-player workshop[/url]). You can also find it on the [url=http://forums.kleientertainment.com/files/file/1108-geometric-placement/]Klei Forums[/url][/h1]
Snaps objects to a grid when placing and displays a build grid around it (unless you hold ctrl).

Credits to zkm2erjfdb and Levorto for writing the original single-player versions (Architectural Geometry and Assisted Geometry). This mod is a replacement for those mods; if you have one of them enabled as well, unpredictable things will happen.

[h1]Configuration Options[/h1]
On the mods screen, with this mod selected, you can change a lot of the settings with the "Configure" button.
[table]
[tr][td][h1]CTRL Turns Grid:[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]On[/u][/b]; the grid is normally off, but holding CTRL shows it[*][b][u]Off[/u][/b]; (default) the grid is normally on, but holding CTRL hides it[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Options Button[/h1][/td][td]A key to open an in-game menu for the mod's options. The default button is B on the keyboard. On controllers, using left stick click while on the scoreboard will open it (you can rebind Menu Misc 3 to change it).[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Toggle Button[/h1][/td][td]A key to toggle between the most recently used geometries (it will guess if it doesn't know, which should only happen if you just transferred between the caves and the surface or joined the game). The default button is V on the keyboard. There is no binding for controllers.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Snap Grid Button[/h1][/td][td]A key to make the grid move to have a point at the object under the cursor, or at key points of a tile (center, edge, corner; technically a 5x5 grid of points within a tile). The default button is unbound on the keyboard, no binding for controllers.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]In-Game Menu[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]On[/u][/b] (default) the options button will bring up the menu.[*][b][u]Off[/u][/b] it will just toggle the mod on and off (like it did before the menu).[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Show Build Grid[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]On[/u][/b] (default) allows the build grid to be shown[*][b][u]Off[/u][/b] never show the build grid[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Grid Geometry[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Square[/u][/b] (default) is the normal grid, aligned with the game's X-Z coordinate system. Hexagonal geometries allow you to do the tightest possible plots.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Refresh Rate[/h1][/td][td][list][*]How much of the available time to use for refreshing the grid. Higher settings will make the grid update faster, but may cause lag.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Hide Cursor Item[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Hide All[/u][/b] when placing things, hide the object so it doesn't cover up the grid[*][b][u]Show Number[/u][/b] hide the object, but keep showing how many you have.[*][b][u]Show All[/u][/b] (default) show the object like usual.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Smart Spacing[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]On[/u][/b] when placing things, the grid spacing adapts to the item being placed; the closest free grid point should always be the closest possible distance.[*][b][u]Off[/u][/b] (default) keep the same spacing for everything.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Fine Grid Size[/h1][/td][td]How many points in each direction the grid should go when placing things that can be tightly packed. Defaults to 10.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Walls Grid Size[/h1][/td][td]How many points in each direction the grid should go when placing walls. Defaults to 6.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Sandbag Grid Size[/h1][/td][td]How many points in each direction the grid should go when placing sandbags. Defaults to 5.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Turf Grid Size[/h1][/td][td]How many tiles in each direction the grid should go when placing turf. Defaults to 2.[/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Grid Colors[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Red/Green[/u][/b] red for "can't place", green for "can place"[*][b][u]Red/Blue[/u][/b] same as red/green, but with blue for "can place"[*][b][u]Black/White[/u][/b] black for "can't place", white for "can place". A bit easier to see at night[*][b][u]Outlined[/u][/b] (default) similar to black/white, but uses black-with-white-outline and white-with-black-outline for the best visibility.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Tighter Chests[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]Yes[/u][/b] allows you to place chests a little bit closer together, like you can with the Architectural or Assisted Geometry mods. Technically the game doesn't normally let you place them quite that close together, but the difference is small. This doesn't work reliably in DST.[*][b][u]No[/u][/b] uses the true spacing for chests.[/list][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][h1]Controller Offset[/h1][/td][td][list][*][b][u]On[/u][/b] uses the normal offset, which rotates with the player.[*][b][u]Off[/u][/b] (default) keeps the object at the player's feet, making it easier to place it right where you want to.[/list][/td][/tr][/table]

publishedfiledetails.title: Craft Pot [DS, ROG, SW, DST]
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
Client mod that adds intuitive cook assisting interface to crock pot.

Doesn't matter what server you join, modded crock pots, modded recipes, this mod serves them all on a plate and helps you cook whatever your heart desires by displaying the exact recipe.
 

[b]What's in this mod:[/b]
- 1. All cooking recipes (INCLUDING MODDED) are listed in a slider next to crock pot;
- 2. Hovering over recipe shows ingredient requirements for it as well as food status of the dish;
- 3. Filling crock pot with ingredients will gradually predict dishes you want to cook;
- 4. Recipe turns green if you put all the required ingredients, just fill crockpot with fillers and it's done;
- 5. Recipe disappears from the list, if you put a bad ingredient;
- 6. Once crockpot is full, the resulting recipe will get painted teal. If you see more than one teal recipe, this means result is unpredictable, cooking will result in one of the highlighted dishes;
- 7. Mod works with any pot that takes 4 ingredients (including warly's portable pot and any modded crockpot)
- 8. You do not need to restart game to make the mod work.
- 9. Full CONTROLLER support

[b]Currently mode has following options:[/b]
- 1. lock uncooked, enabled by default. This option adds a 'recipe lock' simillar to the one in crafting menu, once you cooked an item, the lock disappears and hovering over the dish in the list will show it's hunger/health/sanity values. You may disable and enable it at any time, the progress of cooking will be saved
- 2. Invert controller - by default craftpot scrollbar works with left wiggle (right wiggle used to move items around), checking invert controller makes it work with right wiggle (left wiggle used to move items around).
- 3. Ingredient Popup - by default it is shown, but you can hide it, so that there is only a slider with dishes, no popup with name or stats.

[b]For modders:[/b]
Craftpot exposes the following mod APIs:
1. An API to add images and names for food ingredient tags:
- global 'AddFoodTag' function and a matching FOODTAGDEFINITIONS global dict;
2. An API to registed modded cookpots, for now they do not take extra arguments, but in future they might allow passing custom fields, such as slot number:
- global 'AddCookingPot' function and a matching COOKINGPOTS global dictionary;

It is preferred that during modding you use the provided functions, as they already contain all the safety precautions. But if for some reason the functions are not available during your mod initialization, you can use the dictionaries straight away, but make sure you do not erase the object, that could be prefilled by another mod before you.

[b]DS, ROG, SW version:[/b] http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=662872357

For people off steam, here's a [url=https://github.com/IMalyugin/craftpot]secret link[/url]

中文翻译简介@WendyPan: https://github.com/IMalyugin/craftpot/wiki/chinese

Enjoy :)

ShowMe (this mod) + [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=375859599]Health Info[/url]

[h1]I have to enable only 2 mods?[/h1]
Yes. Actually you can disable all other interface mods and enable only Show Me. But it's better to enable  [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=375859599]Health Info[/url].

[h1]What is better?[/h1][list]
[*]Compared to [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458940297]Item Tooltips[/url] mod my mod provides GREAT network traffic economy: it send info over network ONLY for item under mouse.
[*]But Helath Info mod works faster at the cost of traffic. Health Info is good optimized too but with emphasis on fast delivery of information. So it sends and updates info about health of all creatures around. My mod, on the contrary, saves data traffic, even for the current object.
[/list]

[h1]Details[/h1][list]
[*]There is a little time offset (~100ms) because the mod send info only on mouse over. No waste data traffic.
[*]It will update info not more often than 1 time per 1 second. (For example, Items Tooltips spams RPCs 30 times per second).
[*]Ofc it won't update info if it's not changed. No waste network traffic again. :)
[*]Incompatible with Item Tooltips, Display Food Values and other unknown interface mods.
[*]Compatible with [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=376333686]Combined Status[/url] whose settings will affect temperature units.
[*]Finder mod is included.
[/list]

[h1]Sources[/h1]
[list]
[*]70% of code is taken from [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=369596587]TellMe mod[/url].
[*]20% of code is taken from [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=643193433]Kindling Fire[/url] mod (it has similar hint feature about tinder and striker values).
[/list]

[h1]Languages[/h1]
[list]
[*]English (default)
[*]Russian
[*]Chinese (Simplified and Traditional)
[*]Brazilian Portuguese
[*]Polish
[*]Korean
[*]Spanish
[/list]

[h1]FAQ[/h1]
Q: Is it possible to make a normal Don't Starve version?
A: There is a mod [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=408066317]Detailed Tooltips[/url]. Controller is not supported by that mod.

Q: Is it possible to make client version mod?
A: No, it's not possible. There must be server part of the mod to send information available only on server.

Q: I changed settings but it didn't changed.
A: Client settings are stronger than server settings.
Go to Play->Mods->Server mods->Show Me, and change all values to default.

Q: I got a crash related to game files (like componentactions.lua).
A: ANOTHER mod has a bug with net variables, probably related to containers (e.g. Smarter Crock Pot).

publishedfiledetails.title: Gesture Wheel
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
Adds a wheel selection interface for emotes, making it easier to emote.

By default, the hotkey is set to G (but you can configure it in the mod config options). Holding G will bring up the gesture wheel, then moving your mouse in a particular direction will select a gesture. When you release G, your character will do the gesture.

On controllers, pressing in the left analog activates the wheel, and selection is done by moving the left analog while it's still pressed in (then releasing to make the selection). It's technically bound to Menu Misc 3, which I believe you can rebind in the Controls menu.

I included several options that you might want to change:
[table]
[th][h1][u]Option[/u][/h1][/th][th][h1][u]Description[/u][/h1][/th]
[tr][td][b][h1]Toggle button[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1]Defaults to G, but you can set it to any letter key. Hopefully when mods get proper controls options, this will be nicer to work with :)[/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][b][h1]Wheel Size[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1]Sets the size of the wheel. Defaults to 1, and can be set from 0.1 to 2.[/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][b][h1]Show picture or text[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1]You can have it show just the picture, just the text, or both.[/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][b][h1]Center wheel[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1]Determines whether the wheel comes up around your mouse or the center of the screen.[/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][b][h1]Restore cursor position[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1]If [i]Center Wheel[/i] is disabled, this setting doesn't do anything, unless set to [i]Absolute[/i]. Otherwise:[list][*][i]Relative[/i], the default setting, moves it back where it was before, adding the extra movement you did for the gesture.
[*][i]Absolute[/i] sets it back where it was before without adding the extra movement.
[*][i]Center[/i] sets the mouse to the middle of the wheel when bringing it up, but doesn't move it afterwards.
[*][i]Off[/i] doesn't move the mouse ever.[/list][/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][b][h1]Controller Stick[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1][i]Left[/i] (the default) uses the left analog stick to select emotes, and [i]Right[/i] uses the right stick. If you want to rebind which stick needs to be clicked in, rebind menu_misc_3 in the game's controller controls menu (you'll most likely want to swap it with the scoreboard button).[/h1][/td][/tr]
[tr][td][b][h1]Limit to 8[/h1][/b][/td][td][h1][i]Off[/i] (the default) uses all the emotes, but the wheel is getting pretty crowded (current at 12 emotes), so [i]On[/i] limits the wheel to 8 emotes, which are chosen with the remaining options ([i]Right Emote[/i], [i]Down-Left Emote[/i], and so on).[/h1][/td][/tr][/table]

Things I'd like to add to it:
* Maybe a nice wheel background to make it less floating-in-space-y
* Suggestions?

[b]Thanks to PrzemoLSZ for fixing controller support![/b]

publishedfiledetails.title: Item Info
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
[b]This is a CLIENT mod. Can be used on any server![/b]

Inspired by the popular mods Display Food Values & Detailed Tooltips, I bring you Item Info.

[h1]What this mod does[/h1]
It displays items' values when hovering over them (hunger, sanity, health, spoilage, insulation [winter/summer], light remaining time, waterproof %, sanity gain/min, uses left and damage) via little icons and a value.

Additionally, it can display your equipped items on a panel on the right (configurable), so that you always know your spear's uses, your armor's hp left, or when your torch is going to run out of fuel.

[h1]Configuration Options[/h1]
The default config is just fine, but if you wanna tweak it, here it is:

    Info scale: Sets the tooltip's info scale.
    Time format: Change between hours:minutes:seconds and in-game days.
    Perish info: Set if you only want to see spoilage time, stale time and then spoilage time, or both.
    Show info hands/body/head: If you want to see your equipped items' info.
    Equipped Scale: Set the equipped item's scale, if you think they're too big or too small.
    Show prefab name: If you want to know your items' debug spawn name.
    Show background: If you wanna see a huge, interface-blocking background behind your equipped items.
    Margin bottom/right: To position the equipped item info.


[h1]How to install[/h1]
Just subscribe to the mod. That's it. This mod displays info in a different way to all others, so no need to replace fonts nor anything like that.

[h1]Notes[/h1]
Like other mods, this mod calculates values based on the item's current percent and the base item max values, so the following values might not be 100% exact: perish time, stale time, fuel time, clothes remaining time, uses left, hambat damage.

Controller is supported as of version 0.2

[h1]Current issues[/h1]
There's a bug related to modcomponentactions, which only happens on modded servers, triggered by the way this mod spawns a base item to check its stats. This should make you crash, if you are able to reproduce it please contact me.
Favorite food isn't supported yet.
New characters since Wortox aren't supported yet (foods they won't eat, food bonuses, damage bonuses, etc). I might make some internal changes to add support for them & modded ones someday™


[h1]Latest changes[/h1]
Fixed crash when hovering over trident. Thanks to Grandpa Scout
Fixed equipped items missing. Thanks to 乐十画
Internal changes to pull items' info
Fixed mod not using iceboxes, salt boxes etc. food preserving multiplier
Added salt boxes, Warly's pouch support


If you find a bug, have a suggestion or just like this mod, feel free to leave a comment.
If the mod ever breaks please add me as a friend and nag me every day till I fix it.

publishedfiledetails.title: ActionQueue Reborn
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
This version of Action Queue has been completely rewritten with a focus on fixing all the underlying issues with the previous versions, optimizing and minimizing any performance impact, along with adding several new features. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=609051112]Action Queue DST[/url] ported by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198161551641]xiaoXzzz[/url] has been a great addition to my collection of mods, and it was only after using it for more than a year, that I decided I wanted to undertake fixing the few issues it had.

The original [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=263658444]Action Queue[/url] for Don't Starve by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/nsimplex]simplex[/url], which was created in 2014, is an amazing mod that still sees much use in its various versions.

[h1]Usage[/h1]
[list]
[*]Shift + click on entities as you normally would to add them to the action queue
[*]Shift + double-click on an entity to select all entities of the same prefab in a configurable range
[*]Shift + drag-click a rectangle to select entities within a selection box
[*]Shift + drag-rightclick with a deployable item in your cursor to place it within the bounded area
[*]Shift + drag-rightclick with a tool equipped to focus the actions performed by that tool
[*]Shift + rightclick with a mini-sign in your cursor to place it directly on a chest
[*]Shift + click on a crafting recipe to continuously craft that item
[*]Press C to craft the last completed recipe (includes structures)
[*]Shift + C to continuously craft the last crafted item (doesn't include structures)
[*]Press any movement, primary, secondary, attack, or action key to cancel (or pause) the queue
[*]Press F3 to display a turf grid that may help you with aligning your placements
[*]Press F4 to toggle auto-collect which is triggered by certain actions
[*]Press F5 to toggle endless deploy mode, ignores selection height to deploy all available items
[/list]
[h1]Config Options[/h1]
[list]
[*]ActionQueue key with an extensive keylist
[*]Always clear queue
(if false, use action key(spacebar) to clear selected targets)
[*]Selection color with 10 colors to choose from
[*]Selection opacity
[*]Double click speed
[*]Double click range
[*]Turf grid toggle key
[*]Turf grid radius
[*]Turf grid color
[*]Option to always deploy on the wall / turf grid
[*]Auto-collect toggle key
[*]Enable auto-collect by default
[*]Endless deploy toggle key
[*]Enable endless deploy by default
[*]Craft last recipe key
[*]Tooth-trap spacing
[/list]
[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]Ability to add entities to the selection queue during a deployment action
[*]Auto-collect can be toggled in game as needed
[*]Configurable deploy spacing for tooth traps
[*]Caches your last completed recipe to be re-called with a single key press (default C)
[*]Craft last recipe repeatedly with ActionQueue key + last recipe key (shift + C)
[*]Draw added to the action list
[*]Deploy now goes up and down rows instead of always returning to the horizontal start position
[*]Deployment of items by dropping them on the wall grid
[*]Eat added to the action list
[*]Feedplayer added to the action list
[*]Grabs the next stack of items of the same type from your inventory for active item actions
[*]Heal player added to the action list
[*]Minisigns are now easily placeable on chests
[*]Pick action will never target evil flowers
[*]Pickup action will never target any active trap
[*]Pitchfork actions, digging and placing turf
[*]Repeat crafting is faster (timer based)
[*]Tool filtering, which was a feature of the original mod
[*]Unwrap added to the action list
[*]Waits for a broken tool to re-equip without canceling the queue
[/list]
[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]ActionQueue should never be canceled by using chat, map, or alt-tabbing anymore
[*]ActionQueue now cancels properly if you are moving when you release a mouse button during a selection
[*]Fixed incompatibility with Woodie beaver mode
[*]Deployment is only triggered if the selection queue is empty
[*]Give action now works properly with mushroom planters
[*]Selection will not begin if your first click is on a HUD entity
[*]Significantly improved how actions are applied to their targets
[*]Switched to using control handlers for leftclick and rightclick, which means the mod follows rebinds in the games settings menu for primary and secondary keys
[/list]

[h1]Don't Starve version[/h1]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1930794331]ActionQueue Reborn[/url] by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/myxal]myxal[/url]

publishedfiledetails.title: Fast Travel
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
Build a fast travel network using home signs. You can travel from one home sign to any other home signs instantly.

[h1]Instruction[/h1]
- Right click on a home sign to select destination. Right click repeatedly to cycle through all available destinations. After having selected a destination, stay close to the home sign to travel.
- Fast travel costs hunger and sanity just like normal travel. [u]The cost is directly proportional to the distance travelled, and is configurable.[/u] The cost is shown when you select a destination. Travelling in summer costs 25% less sanity; travelling in winter costs 25% more sanity.

[b]Group Travel[/b]
Each individual in a group should right-click the same home sign once. Let the last person select the destination. Then stay close to the home sign to fast travel.

[b]Cancel Travel[/b]
Just walk away and stay away from any home signs. Your travel will be cancelled in 15 seconds.

[b]Ownership Restriction[/b]
If you have installed the Ownership mod, you can apply ownership restriction through configuration option (disabled by default). A player cannot travel from or travel to a home sign he doesn’t own (private home signs won’t appear on destination list).

[b]Other Restrictions[/b]
A player may not fast travel if:
- The home sign at destination is destroyed before departure.
- His/her character is dead or is a ghost.
- His/her character is still in combat or is near danger.
- His/her character doesn’t have enough hunger or sanity.

[b]Notes[/b]
- Arrow signs are not part of fast travel network.
- Describe/Name your home signs sensibly. The name/description is later used to identify the destination.
- The maximum travel distance per trip is 1640 units. In a default DST world, you might not be able to travel from one corner of the map to the opposite corner in one single trip (it normally requires 1 stop).
- This mod works with existing world and home signs that are already built. However, you cannot rename signs.
- There is no map interface integration.

publishedfiledetails.title: Campfire Respawn
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
Allows you to respawn, when you haunt campfires.
Works the same way as the Jury-Rigged Portal.

Enabled by default to Respawn by :
[list]
    [*] Campfire
    [*] Firepit
    [*] Endothermic Fire
    [*] Endothermic Fire Pit
[/list]

Only works in Endless and Survival mode.

You can toggle everything on/off as you please.

[h3]Additional Features[/h3]
All these below are disabled by default.
[b]Resurrectors[/b]
[list]
    [*] Skeleton
        Respawn when you Haunt a Skeleton or Player Skeleton.
        
    [*] Telltale Heart
        Respawn when you Haunt a Telltale Heart that lies on the ground. Consumes the Heart.
        
    [*] Use Tags
        Blocks all other Campfire settings, uses the "campfire" tag to add the resurrection mechanic to all prefabs with that tag.
        This should make the mod work with other mods, aslong as their prefabs have that tag.
[/list]

[b]Health Penalties[/b]
[list]
    [*] Generic
        Health penalty when respawning by a Telltale Heart, used by a player on a ghost.

    [*] Portal
        Health penalty when respawning by the Jury-Rigged Portal.

    [*] Generic Max
        The max percentage of health the player can lose from penalties.

    [*] Campfire
        Health penalty when respawning by a Campfire

    [*] Skeleton
        Health penalty when respawning by a Skeleton

    [*] Attunement - Meat Effigy
        Amount of Health it cost to Attune at a Meat Effigy.
        
    [*] Health Respawn Amount
        How much Health can the player respawn with? This is a base value that'll be affected by other vanilla modifiers. Health can never be above the characters Max Health.
[/list]

[b]Extra Features[/b]
[list]
    [*] Return Hotkey
		Will return you to the last place you respawned or the Jury-Rigged Portal. Does not work inbetween loads.
        [list]
            [*] Last : Will try to respawn you at the Last place you respawned at, does not work inbetween loads.
            [*] Closest : Will try to find the Closest place you can respawn, doesn't work with the Meat Effigy, Telltale Hearts, Skeletons. Max Range is 1000.
        [/list]
        If either option fails, you'll be respawned at the Jury-Rigged Portal, unless in Survival mode where you can't respawn using the portal.

    [*] Kill Me
        Kill bind that kills you when you press it, only possible while your character has the 'idle' animation tag.

    [*] Respawn Me
        Respawn bind that respawns you when you press it, only possible while your ghost character has the 'idle' animation tag.

    [*] No Player Skeletons
        Players Won't drop Skeletons when they die. Actually the skeleton will instantly get removed when it spawns but you shouldn't be able to notice it.
        This will also remove any existing player skeletons in the world too!

    [*] Spawn Protection
        When Haunting to Respawn, you'll get Spawn Protection like Griefer Spawn Protection.

    [*] Keep Inventory
        Don't drop anything on death. Except for WX-78's installed modules.
        
    [*] Keep Inventory - Bug Fix
        Fixes a bug where when respawning by haunting and having 'Keep Inventory' enabled, the player's hat will not be visible. The fix seems to work most of the time.
[/list]

publishedfiledetails.title: Insight (Show Me+)
publishedfiledetails.file_description:
[h1]Thank you for 1 million subscribers![/h1]
I never expected this many users. Thank you for your support!

[h1]Background Information[/h1]
Inspired by Show Me.
Because I like to know everything about everything. Show me was nice, but it was inaccurate/weird for some things and just didn't have what I was looking for.
This was coded from scratch, and I originally made it for DS. I ported it over!

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2081254154][b]Click for DS Version[/b][/url]

[h1]Details[/h1]
Whereas some mods provide information only on inspection, this provides a tooltip with various information on mouse over. Information is cached for items in your active area (Klei has this set to about 2 screens length) and seeks to find a balance between efficiency and convenience.

[h3]Server/Client Configuration[/h3]
Clients and servers share most of the options, with some being exclusive to the client. By default, [u]undefined[/u] options are chosen which means the client can choose what they want. Otherwise, the server has authority. 

Server Configuration: [u]Main Menu -> Host Game[/u] -> Mods -> Server Mods -> Insight -> Configure Mod
Client Configuration: [u]Main Menu -> Mods[/u] -> Server Mods -> Insight -> Configure Mod

[i]A lot of this stuff is controlled in the mod configuration. In general, if it has to do with HOW the information is displayed, it's a client setting. If it has to do with the information itself, it's a server setting.[/i]

[h3]Features[/h3]
[list]
[*][b][u]Controller Support[/u][/b]
[*]Farm Information
[*]Text coloring
[*]Icon Mode
[*]Attack ranges
[*]Health
[*]Damage
[*]Fuel
[*]Food Value
[*]Durability
[*]Chest/Item/Bundle Highlighting
[*]Item/Cookbook Lookups
[*]Naughtiness
[*][u][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=376333686]Combined Status[/url] Integration[/u] (for [u]Naughtiness[/u] and corrected moon cycles)
[*]Follower Info
[*][i]Most things, really.[/i]
[/list]

[h1]FAQ[/h1]
[h3]Is this a server mod? Can you make a client mod version of this?[/h3]
[b][i][u]This is a server mod[/u][/i][/b].
A client-side version of this mod would have almost none of the information this mod displays. The server contains almost everything. That's why this is a server mod.

[h3]How do I turn <thing> off?[/h3]
Pretty much everything can be configured to turn on, off, or adjust the level of detail. If you can't find a configuration option from the main menu, you can double check the in-game configuration menu (Insight Menu -> Config Button).

[h3]There's too much information! I'm overwhelmed![/h3]
I've gotten feedback that the amount of information Insight provides can be overwhelming, or that it's too much effort to adjust all the configs. Insight now comes with some presets to adjust configurations in bulk:
[list]
[*][u]New Player[/u] - Recommended for new players, configured for a tiny amount of information to allow them the "authentic vanilla" experience.
[*][u]Simple[/u] - Recommended for players who liked Show Me's limited amount of information.
[*][u]Decent[/u] - More or less the default configuration layout with a few tweaks.
[*][u]Advanced[/u] - Recommended for players who like having a lot of information available.
[/list]
You can access these presets by going to the in-game Insight Menu -> Configure Mod -> Presets. Detected first-time users will be prompted to select a preset when first playing with Insight.

[h1]Feedback[/h1]
Feel free to suggest features or provide feedback, good or bad. This mod is still being developed, so it's possible for issues to occur. If you do encounter one, please check the bug reporting discussion post [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/discussion/2189004162/2793873675751084957/]here.[/url]
[b]You can also enable the automatic crash reporter, which will try to report your crashes for you.[/b]
Also, check out [url=https://support.klei.com/hc/en-us/articles/360029881191-Logs-and-Useful-Information-for-Bug-Reports-for-Don-t-Starve-Together]this link from Klei[/url] for advice on finding logs & submitting bugs.
